paragraphs.text: Palagano et al. (2018) used exome sequencing to study an Indian family with 2 sibs affected by acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis. In the patients they found a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the NBAS gene. The NBAS protein has been implicated in 2 cellular processes: nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic. Both processes were impaired in HEK293T cells overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein, as shown by real-time PCR, Western blot analysis, coimmunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence analysis. Immunohistochemistry of mouse embryos at different developmental stages detected NBAS expression in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton, and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum.
